title: Daybreak onprem tunnel triage — weeknote
content:
Week summary (May 3–10, 2027)

Context:
- Customer: Arcturus Health (large onprem VPC deployment, HIPAA scope).
- Current phase: final network handoff + canary traffic (2 nodes) before scale roll.
- Primary blockers surfaced this week: encrypted tunnel flaps, MTU mismatch across their transit, and intermittent telemetry blackhole from canary node CAN-2.

Daily standup highlights (abridged):
- 2027-05-03 09:05 — Maya: kicked off tunnel re-provision with on-site network engineer (Nina). Observed odd MSS clamping on their edge firewall. Filed INFRA-2741.
- 2027-05-04 09:20 — Diego: Canary CAN-2 dropped connection after 12:40 UTC during customer failover test. Syslogs show duplicate sequence numbers on IPsec SA teardown. Added tcpdump capture to PD-498.
- 2027-05-05 09:15 — Priya: Verified BGP neighbors stable but saw asymmetric path causing MTU from 1500 -> 1400 on one leg; packets >1400 fragmented, causing our runtime gRPC streams to reset. Raised with customer NOC.
- 2027-05-06 10:00 — Samir: Confirmed that our KV cache warmups were succeeding but metrics ingestion to telemetry pipeline missing for ~30 minutes due to proxy TLS altname mismatch. Short-term: we reverted to UDP-based stats forwarder for CAN-2.
- 2027-05-07 11:30 — Incident scrub: decided to hold full rollout. Need two successful 24h canary windows with stable telemetry and zero tunnel resets.

Actions (owners + deadlines):
- Diego — complete in-depth ipsec SA dump analysis and upload filtered pcap to PD ticket (INFRA-2741). Due 2027-05-11.
- Priya — coordinate MTU adjustment with Arcturus NOC and request scheduled maintenance window for path MTU probe (PD-498). Due 2027-05-12.
- Maya — create temporary port-forward play (ssh jump -> relay) and a howto for field engineers to get quick console access in case of ipsec flaps. Draft by 2027-05-06 (done), review with SRE by 2027-05-10.
- Samir — restore telemetry via alternate TLS cert chain (workaround) and instrument extra metrics to detect sequence restarts. Patch PR: ops#987. Target 2027-05-09.
- Solutions Eng (Priya + Diego) — schedule customer deep-dive (90m) to walk through packet captures and routing diagrams. Meeting target: 2027-05-11.

Short technical notes and findings:
- Tunnel flap pattern: flaps correlate with their onprem backup router failover. When HSRP toggles, our IPsec endpoints attempt SA rekeying and sometimes race, producing duplicate packets and sequence resets. Potential fix paths: tune lifetime/reauth jitter, or enable route-based standby with deterministic preemption on their side.
- MTU: fragmentation plus DF (don't fragment) on the customer's transit caused gRPC resets. Suggested immediate mitigation: lower our internal egress MSS to 1360 for this customer. Long term: align MTU across both transit legs.
- Telemetry: CAN-2 TLS handshake failing due to customer TLS middlebox rewriting SNI. We bypassed by using TLS certificate with SAN containing their proxy alias; longer-term ask: terminate at the proxy with proper header passthrough.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: Rollout while tunnel instability persists -> user requests timeouts and duplicate charges. Severity: high. Mitigation: block rollout until 48h stable.
- Risk: Fixing MTU reduces throughput for encrypted large-payloads -> cost/perf impact. Severity: medium. Mitigation: measure token cost delta in canary.
- Risk: Workaround cert chain leads to audit questions (HIPAA) -> escalates to security/compliance. Severity: high. Mitigation: document change, run compliance review, get signoff from security.

Open questions / things to escalate:
- Should we prefer route-based IPsec (VTI) or policy-based for this class of customer? (Note: customer-run edge prefers policy-based historically). Decision link: Confluence PD decision thread.
- Do we require runbook changes for night-shift engineers for quick MTU/MSS rollbacks? (We have a one-liner script but it needs permission gating).
- Is HSM/KMS integration for onprem still in scope for this sprint? Arcturus asked for HSM-backed key wrap for their encryption-at-rest; SRE says low priority until network stable.

Customer comms draft (to be sent after triage):
"Hi Arcturus team — we surfaced 3 network-related issues blocking the rollout: asymmetric MTU, IPsec SA race during your backup router failover, and a telemetry handshake rewrite at your edge. We propose the following immediate steps: (1) short maintenance window to run MTU probes and set consistent MTU, (2) apply temporary MSS clamp on our egress for the canary, and (3) schedule 90m joint packet-capture deep dive. Let us know availability for 2027-05-11. — Maya / RDW Install"

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Add jitter to rekey timers in next ipsec configuration template (small change, test in lab).
- Create a checklist entry: "confirm SNI passthrough" under day-two playbooks. Saw this bite twice now.
- Thinking: automate canary reimage + telemetry smoke test that runs immediately after BGP flaps. Could cut time-to-detect by ~40%.

Attachments / useful links:
- packet capture excerpts (attached to INFRA-2741)
- CAN-2 metrics dump (S3 link in PD-498)
- ops PR: https://github.com/redwood/ops/pull/987 (telemetry cert work)
- Customer runbook snippet: Confluence page 37624

Next check-in cadence:
- Twice-daily brief (09:00 UTC and 17:00 UTC) until both canaries complete 48h windows.
- Full retro and playbook updates planned for next Wed (2027-05-12).

If anything odd appears outside those windows ping #vpc-installs and escalate to oncall-sre.

-- Maya
